# sharness.ai — SHarness

> SHarness runs agents and their tools as small, single-purpose processes, each locked down by
> the kernel and talking only over allowed, mutually authenticated connections, so a secret
> lives in one place and a tricked process can only do its one job.

Site version: v0.6.30. Status of the project: DESIGN, with the first experiments RUNNABLE (E01 to E04,
E05, E09 and E10 in the CLI; E09 is a real Linux kernel in a browser tab running hello, measured 25 Oct 2026),
and MVPs on the CLI's dev branch: the levels (contain, profile, explain), the first door,
sharness.fs (a Setting) and, as of 28 Oct 2026, the network door sharness.net with the launcher's first slice,
`sharness-ai shell` (a Boundary only for the shell it starts). No other SHarness component is built.
By Dinis Cruz; design session written up with Claude, 24 October 2026. All content CC BY 4.0.
SHarness is unrelated to Sharness, the shell testing library.

## Properties agents may rely on

- Every claim is labelled. MEASURED means probed or timed in one Claude agent workspace on
  24 Oct 2026, with method on /evidence/. Everything else is DESIGNED or PROPOSED. "Not yet
  measured" items are listed on /evidence/. The site never claims a component is a Boundary before the launcher exists, never
  claims protection against root or kernel compromise, and says nothing about any platform's
  plans.
- Every design page is available as markdown at the same path: /<page>/index.md. The markdown
  is the SOURCE; the HTML is generated from it (tools/gen_pages.py) and CI fails if they
  drift.
- The source design pack is published verbatim under /project/sources/sharness-brief-pack/ (the brief
  for this site plus docs 00–07). Docs 01–04 use sgit-specific names: sgit-kms →
  sharness.kms, sgit-net → sharness.net, sgit-fs → sharness.fs, sgit-cli → the harnessed app.
- /llms-full.txt is this file plus every page's markdown in one fetch, GENERATED.
- The version in /tools/version.txt agrees with every page badge, this file,
  /llms-full.txt and /index.md: the pre-release gate fails the release otherwise.

## Sections (the site was restructured on 25 Oct 2026; every old address redirects)

- /design/ — the design: the brief and the design pages
- /code/ — where the code is, the CLI, experiments, flows, examples, languages
- /evidence/ — measurements, what exists today, the research note
- /security/ — the project's own account of its security: threat model, known risks, reviews, hardening, supply chain
- /landscape/ — policies at the centre: the thesis, the enforceability matrix, integration points, the market
- /explain/ — storyboards and mockups; /articles/ — the articles
- /project/ — about, the source documents (verbatim), engineering, comms, releases, the agents and their keys, outreach, telemetry
- /admin/ — how the project is run: the board, the members, the updates, status, the guidance for agents

## The design (read in this order)

- /design/index.md — THE BRIEF: SHarness in one read, with four drawn diagrams (the moving parts,
  one request end to end, the whole surface of a process, the spectrum). READ THIS FIRST
- /design/why/index.md — the last metre: a sealed vault key exposed on arrival (disk, argv, the
  transcript); goals; threat model (kernel trusted; root out of scope)
- /design/architecture/index.md — the components and the edge matrix (deny by default; the app
  never talks to the KMS); mutual TLS 1.3 with a session CA whose key is destroyed after issuing;
  measured costs (~3.2 ms per handshake); deployment topologies A–E
- /design/components/index.md — sharness.launcher, .kms, .net, .fs, .bash, .llm, .policy: one job,
  one uid, one policy, one certificate each; transparent vs harness-aware apps; size targets
- /design/keys/index.md — the sealed handover; the KMS protocol (init, public, unwrap, seal_to,
  destroy); sealing to one-time keys; binding a remote caller; where the private key lives
- /design/policies/index.md — Process Behaviour Policies: ABP (mandate, grant, delta, barrier)
  applied to processes; intersection-composed layers; the one hash the person supplies; the
  enforcement map; learning a policy from strace; prompt-injection walkthrough; the v0 shape
- /design/pbp/index.md — THE PBP ON ONE PAGE: the definition every page and enforcer is checked against;
  the four objects for a process; text + hash from outside + an enforcer the subject does not include;
  capability rows (kernel) and behaviour rows (keeper) and the precondition rule that joins them; the
  four parts of the spec (schema, hash, composition, conformance). PROPOSED, 25 Oct 2026
- /design/levels/index.md — THE LEVELS: six levels of one policy (intent, profiles, rows in plain nouns,
  doors and targets, mechanisms, the ground), each compiling deterministically into the one below so the
  simplest is as binding as the deepest; every level reports unheld rows in its own nouns; an escape hatch
  to any lower level; each level a service (vendor, organisation, laptop); two stacks on TCP. PROPOSED, 26 Oct 2026
- /design/decision/index.md — THE DECISION AT THE DOOR: the permission prompt as a Setting and a bad decision (ux.sgit.ai
  UX-059); the prompt as the last resort (yes to what the policy allows, silence for what it refuses, a question only
  for what it cannot hold); the decision engine: command + policy + intent -> allow, deny or ask, unknown is no, an
  approved ask is a learned row; a Setting at a hook, a Boundary in sharness.bash; a 99-line prototype on twelve
  commands; two measurements (the terminal's devices as write rows; a learned policy is never trimmed by hand). PROPOSED, 26 Oct 2026
- /design/agents/index.md — how an agent message flowed in the observed workspace; where SHarness
  plugs in (hooks documented; Claude Code's own sandbox); sharness.llm; sharness.bash; dual-LLM
- /design/process-tree/index.md — making every process go through sharness.bash; side doors;
  safety rules for testing in a live session. PROOF OF CONCEPT NOT YET RUN
- /design/surface/index.md — what a process can do: the whole surface, one row per interface,
  what bounds each, measured or not, what is not covered; a virtual operating system for one process
- /design/containment/index.md — can every process be constrained, memory included; how far
  hostile code inside is held, by threat class; defence in depth; where a microVM belongs
- /design/spectrum/index.md — five profiles from a hello world (runnable) to sgit (harness-aware);
  the compatibility map for sgit's next version; two sgit commands measured under a v0 policy
- /design/roadmap/index.md — decided, open decisions (1–11), the refactor path in sgit, the end
  state, and ground rules for the agents that will build SHarness

## The code (RUNNABLE: experiments E01 to E05, E09, E10 and three MVPs in the CLI; two doors, sharness.fs and sharness.net, run as MVPs)

- /components/index.md — the components as the operating system a process sees: five doors (fs, net, kms, bash, llm) and
  the bootstrap, each a small REST service on loopback with mutual TLS; everything is a request with a verdict;
  pick one (each is worth adopting alone); start with bash. One page per component: /components/<name>/index.md
  (bash, net, kms, fs, llm, launcher, policy), each with the API (proposed), the requests and their verdicts, what
  it enforces with what, what it does not do
- /code/index.md — where everything is: the package module by module (with line counts), the
  commands, what on this site has code behind it and what does not, next in order
- /code/cli/index.md — the sharness-ai package: what exists (PyPI v0.1.0 vs dev), the first version
  as proposed, the v0 policy and its hash, naming, versioning, releases
- /code/experiments/index.md — the ladder: browser mockups, any Claude session, Linux, planned,
  the launcher above the agent; E01 to E10; E04 and E09 measured; the example policies P0 to P4
  (a hello world, an agent session, a tool server, the newsroom agent, sgit); what Claude Code's own sandbox gives
- /code/flows/index.md — what happens, module by module, when run confines a command and when
  hello runs; the hash in two implementations; what the launcher adds (designed)
- /code/examples/index.md — every command with its output; sgit under a policy; the skill
- /code/browser/index.md — Linux in the browser (E09, built and measured 25 Oct 2026): one Alpine x86 guest
  with Alpine's Landlock kernel runs hello 6 of 6 under v86 in Node, in a browser tab and through chroot on
  the host kernel; the page is /code/browser/demo/index.html; the research, the options, what a browser never shows
- /code/playground/index.html — the playground (HTML only): sharness-ai in Pyodide (pip install, hash, check,
  translate; run and hello refuse with no kernel) and in a shell on the Linux guest (enforced); one policy hashed three ways
- /articles/linux-in-a-tab.md — the milestone: a real kernel enforcing a Process Behaviour Policy in Chrome,
  what held where, what did not work (the ELF interpreter needs the execute right), how it fits together
- /code/releases/index.md — the code at immutable paths: /code/releases/releases.json (every release),
  /code/releases/latest.json and latest/ (the newest), /code/releases/vN/vN.M/vN.M.P/manifest.json (sha256 and
  sha384 integrity for every file; the source commit), /code/releases/dev/ (a snapshot, no promise)
- /code/languages/index.md — Python first; Rust for the KMS and the bash client; JSON for policies; the
  proposed set of reference implementations (JavaScript in Node and the browser, Go, Rust; Java, .NET, C later)
- /code/standards/index.md — the standards and their reference implementations: the registry (policy v0 written; the
  acceptance test, the manifest, the protocols to come); one row per implementation with what it passes and who reviewed it
- /code/standards/policy-v0/index.md — the first standard: the v0 shape, canonical JSON, the sha256 hash, what is
  refused so every language hashes the same, the environment contract; /code/standards/policy-v0/vectors.json lists
  the 28 test vectors (13 accept with their hashes, 15 refuse) that Python, JavaScript and Go pass
- /articles/one-standard-many-languages.md — by dev@sharness: what in each component is a standard and what is
  an implementation; the component-by-language map; what each runtime adds to the attack surface; the
  adoption ladder from a policy file to a component; standards versioned with vectors and a reviewed registry

## Security (the register; nothing reviewing SHarness should find what it does not already say)

- /security/index.md — the hub: the five pages, where the first review stands (25 findings on 25 Oct 2026:
  5 High, 7 Medium, 11 Low, 2 Info; all High fixed), how to report, what the section does not do
- /security/threat-model/index.md — assets, actors, the two trust boundaries (the person's hash; the kernel),
  surface by surface what the code of today holds, what the designed launcher adds, what nothing covers
- /security/risks/index.md — the register, SR-01 to SR-27 and the design's SD rows: weight, state (fixed /
  accepted / open / designed), the reason and the test. Accepted: Unix-domain sockets by path (Landlock has
  no rule), Pyodide from a CDN without integrity. Open: the environment row (SR-11, board R16), the repository
  settings (SR-24, board R15)
- /security/reviews/index.md — review 1, 25 Oct 2026: scope, method, environment, SF-01 to SF-25 with the fix
  and the test, what was examined and found clean, what was not examined
- /security/hardening/index.md — how to run sharness-ai so it holds as much as it can; the lock-down list
  for the organisation, both repositories, PyPI, Pages and the agents (settings only a person can change)
- /security/supply-chain/index.md — no dependencies; every action pinned by commit; the release path (build
  and publish separated, Trusted Publishing, PEP 740 attestations); what the site loads from elsewhere;
  the code published at immutable paths under /code/releases/ with manifests, a latest and a dev snapshot
- /.well-known/security.txt — the contact (GitHub private vulnerability reporting)

## Evidence and status

- /evidence/index.md — every measurement with method, date and caveats; §9 the first experiments
  run by the CLI; what is documented but not exercised; what is not measured
- /evidence/status/index.md — what exists today and what does not (the honest column)
- /evidence/machines/index.md — hello on your machine: every reported run of sharness-ai hello (kernel, Landlock
  ABI, uid, Python, result), failures first; how to report yours with hello --json
- /evidence/research/index.md — the published design read in full on 24 Oct 2026: ten findings
  and what was done about each; what is still open and in what order

## The landscape (SHarness as the reference implementation of Process Behaviour Policies)

- /landscape/index.md — the thesis in four steps: a policy says what a process may do (ABP → PBP);
  SHarness is one enforcer, built to be read; any environment that enforces the same rows is
  valid, so enforcers mix and match under one hash; every product is an integration point or a
  translation target; the three questions (express, enforce as what barrier kind, verify)
- /landscape/enforceability/index.md — the matrix: policy rows × enforcers (SHarness, bubblewrap,
  Docker, Claude Code's sandbox, Kubernetes, microVMs, ToolHive, OpenShell) with the barrier kind
  per cell; `sharness-ai policy translate` writes four of the columns and prints the gap (E10)
- /landscape/integrations/index.md — product by product: what it stands in for, what a policy
  translates into, what SHarness adds, what to keep
- /landscape/ruflo/index.md — Ruflo (formerly Claude Flow) and rUv's stack in SHarness's terms;
  what ruv.sgit.ai integrated (an ABP per agent compiled into Ruflo's policy engine, memory in
  sgit vaults); the integration points table; a swarm under the harness; what to do first
- /landscape/market/index.md — market and competitive analysis as of 24 Oct 2026: sandboxes and
  runtimes, guardrails, MCP and tool security, LLM gateways, secrets and identity, enterprise
  platforms, standards; every row sourced; where SHarness sits; threats to the thesis

## Project

- /project/adoption/index.md — getting users: the review of the site from a user's angle, what changed, who
  the users are, where to find them, how to tell whether it is working
- /project/about/index.md — identity and naming rules: brand SHarness; command sharness-ai (never
  plain sharness); env prefix SHARNESS_AI_; components sharness.<role>; who writes here
- /project/sources/index.md — the source documents, verbatim, with known issues; the pack at
  /project/sources/sharness-brief-pack/ and the memos at /project/sources/memos/
- /project/engineering.html — how the site is built; /project/comms.html — open requests (R3 the
  design pages need review; R6 the research note, experiments, cast, market analysis, containment;
  R7 releasing the CLI's dev to main; R8 the languages decision; R9 to R11 the sherpa agent's key, access
  token and the go on outreach); /project/releases.html — the release history
- /project/agents/index.md — the agents and their keys: cli@sharness, dev@sharness and sherpa@sharness, their
  keys on pki.sgit.ai, the vault register (ids, never keys), how a secret reaches an agent and a key reaches Dinis
- /project/outreach/index.md — the outreach plan (a PLAN, nothing posted yet), the companion of
  /project/adoption/: what there is to show, five audiences and their sentence, the channels (repository,
  lists, Show HN, Reddit, LinkedIn, ruv.sgit and the Agentics Foundation, OWASP, the sandbox people,
  directories, the network), the rules, thirty days, the measures
- /project/telemetry/index.md — who reads this site: one anonymous event per page per session over an
  append lane, encrypted in the browser; what is sent, never sent; the lane waits on an access token (R10)

## Admin: how the project is run (public, like everything here)

- /admin/index.md — the hub: how work moves (a request, a board row, a branch, a release, an update, a debrief), the members
- /admin/board/index.md — THE BOARD: every request to the editor (R) and every task (T), numbered, with owner and status;
  one file per row under content/admin/board/; the same table at /project/comms.html
- /admin/members/index.md — who does what: one person and the agents, each with a role, a behaviour policy and a status
  of its own at /admin/members/<id>/index.md (conductor, editor, cli@sharness, dev@sharness, sherpa)
- /admin/updates/index.md — UPDATES: what is happening, dated, newest first; each at /admin/updates/<id>/index.md
- /admin/notes/index.md — COMMIT NOTES (Commit-FS-lite): every commit on both repositories' dev since 24 Oct 2026
  with its Agent: line and its To-<member>: notes, newest first; the agents' conversation, in the open
- /admin/schedule/index.md — SCHEDULE: every member that runs on its own, its card (wakes in London time, cron, the
  start prompt for a new session on any Claude account, the wake prompt word for word); how to set a member up anywhere
- /admin/runs/index.md — every run a member recorded; a missing record is a missed wake
- /admin/briefs/index.md — every brief, published in full before the work; each at /admin/briefs/<slug>/index.md
- /admin/status/index.md — where every branch of both repositories is, and every member; a snapshot from git
- /admin/guidance/index.md — AGENTS.md: the rules every agent works by, on both repositories; how to join
